# Glossary

**Status:** active
**Category:** E (product / user)
**Created:** 2026-10-31
**Last updated:** 2026-10-31
**Owner:** TCS team

<!-- Source for the published wiki page. Generated by scripts/publish-public-docs.cjs — edit here. -->

The ten words that make everything else readable. The app has its **own** glossary of 99 entries across
12 categories at `/education/glossary`; this page is the shorthand for reading the code and the issues.

| Term | Means | Does **not** mean |
|---|---|---|
| **Directive** | One scoring rule with its own `maxScore`. "RSI oversold", "earnings surprise", "session timing" | A filter or a gate — it contributes points, it does not refuse |
| **Protocol** | A named selection of directives plus thresholds. The unit you score with | A trading strategy — it produces scores, not orders |
| **Score / composite** | The sum of a protocol's directive scores. Unbounded by design | A percentage. The 0–100 in the UI is normalised for display only |
| **Gate** | A pass/fail check applied *after* scoring: threshold, session, liquidity, risk, capability | Part of the score — a gate cannot raise it |
| **Bot** | A record binding **protocol + symbol + sizing + limits + mode** | An algorithm. It has no logic of its own; it is configuration |
| **Protocol subscription** | The link that makes a bot receive signals for a protocol | Implied by having a protocol — a bot without one is never queued |
| **Envelope** | The proposed trade: side, size, stop, target, derived from the score and the bot | A placed order |
| **Signal** | A gated, scored candidate that survived every check | A recommendation, or a promise |
| **Decision trail** | The recorded chain trade → dispatch → gate → score → directive → data | A log file — it is a queryable object |
| **A/B pair** | Two copied configurations run side by side to answer *"which is better?"* | A backtest. It is live, and it needs a sample before it will name a winner |

## Modes

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| `auto` | The bot dispatches on the automation loop |
| `semi-auto` / `manual` | The bot may compute, but does not dispatch by itself |
| **Paper / demo** | An account the broker identifies as not holding real money |
| **`accountKind`** | The app's name for demo / contest / real, read from the terminal. ⚠️ Never called `tradeMode`, which already means two other things |

## The phrase you will see in code comments

> **"Plausible output, no error."**

The signature of this project's most expensive defects: a stale symbol returns a score, a mis-sized
trade returns a fill, a wrong denominator returns a percentage — and nothing throws. When you see a
`CANNOT JUDGE`, a `null` kept distinct from `0`, or an explicit *"unverified"* in a comment, that
phrase is the reason.
